expected_level_description: You can: - manage the monthly reporting cycle for a directorate or programme - build cost models, such as the full cost of a digital service or the unit cost of a transaction - analyse spending trends and advise managers on actions to stay within budget - challenge budget holders constructively on their forecasts

You can: - lead budget setting and forecasting for a directorate or large programme - model scenarios and sensitivities, such as inflation, delays, or changes in funding - build multi-year forecasts for digital programmes, including the running costs that follow investment - present forecasts and risks to senior managers

You can: - build the financial model for a straightforward business case - separate capital and revenue costs, and one-off and recurring costs - include whole-life costs, such as licences, support, and hosting after go-live

You can: - apply the organisation's capital and revenue rules to everyday spending - explain how funding allocations and spending limits affect your area - recognise spending that needs approval from a funder or spending control
You can: - use spreadsheets well, including formulas, lookups, and pivot tables - maintain finance system data, such as cost centres, suppliers, and approvers - report and help fix system problems
You can: - balance cost versus value - consider the impact of user needs - report on financial delivery - monitor cost and budget - understand how and when to escalate issues

You can: - identify important stakeholders and communicate with them clearly and regularly - tailor communication to stakeholders' needs and work with them to build relationships while meeting user needs - build and reach consensus with stakeholders - work to improve stakeholder relationships using evidence to explain decisions

You can: - listen to the needs of design and business stakeholders and interpret information - take part in discussions within a multidisciplinary team - be an advocate for the team externally, and can manage differing perspectives - shape and share communications relevant to the audience

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
